key_insight: PING uses a physics-informed graph neural network to forecast transport dynamics on irregular sensor networks and support improved solar power forecasting.
engineering_relevance: Better intra-day PV power forecasts can support grid integration of solar generation without changing solar cell hardware.
method: Represent advection-diffusion particle concentrations as signals on a graph.
Add a discretized advection-diffusion equation as a soft constraint in the training loss.
Couple PING with PV forecasting models using ground-based sensor data and satellite-derived cloud information.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports performance on par with state-of-the-art models on synthetic and real transport datasets, including sea surface temperature and cloud index data, and improved intra-day PV forecasts through hybrid modeling.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical forecast gains, and a soft physics constraint does not guarantee physically consistent predictions.
paper_title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting
